extracted.intended_audience: readers of late-19th-century social fiction; writers studying social satire and scene-setting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for depicting upper-class social gatherings, characters, and ironic narrator commentary in social-satire/realist fiction. Emphasizes atmospheric detail, contrasts between artificiality and nature, characterization through gesture and dialogue, and satirical voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depicting an aristocratic 'crush' / 'at home'
rubrics_metrics.description: Who can adequately describe the thrilling excitement attending an aristocratic 'crush,'--an extensive, sweeping-off-of-old-cores 'at home,'--that scene of bewildering confusion ...? Who can paint in sufficiently brilliant colors the mere outside of a house thus distinguished by this strange festivity ...?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List concrete, visible elements to evoke the occasion: crowding of carriages; shouting of small boys and policemen; contention between pompous coachmen and good-natured cabbys; striped awning avenue lined with tropical verdure; illumination with Chinese lanterns. Use these recognizable set-pieces to create the spectacle and social significance of an 'at home.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of artificial spectacle as contrast to nature
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk of orange groves in Italy and the languid light of a southern moon! What are they compared to the marvels of striped awning? Mere trees--mere moonlight--(poor products of Nature!) do not excite either wonder or envy--but, strange to say, an awning avenue invariably does!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit contrast between 'borrowed' artifices and natural beauty to satirize taste and pretension. Emphasize how manufactured decorations (awnings, hired foliage, lanterns) provoke social envy and attention more readily than genuine natural splendor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show different social classes' responses to spectacle
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as [awnings are erected] ... the beggar, starving for a crust, lingers doubtfully near it ... If Awning Avenue means matrimony, the beggar waits to see the guests come out; if ... some evening festivity, he goes, resolving to return at the appointed hour ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict how a single event or ornament reverberates across classes: the curious street-arabs and nursemaids, the hungry beggar imagining supper, the envious powerless who dream of such abundance. Use a few focused vignettes to show social contrast and moral implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convey social boredom and performative manners via small details
rubrics_metrics.description: Gentlemen of serious demeanor, who are leaning, as though exhausted, against the banisters, with a universal air of profound weariness and dissatisfaction ... a trained opera-singer is shaking forth chromatic roulades ... there is a never-ending monotonous hum of voices, only broken at rare intervals by the 'society laugh'--that unmeaning giggle ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use posture, repetitive actions (leaning, yawning), background amusements (opera singer, perfumed air), and the mechanical 'society laugh' to show that the festive surface hides ennui and performativity. Small recurring motifs (yawns, forced giggles) dramatize emptiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization through small domestic gestures and interior thoughts
rubrics_metrics.description: She kissed a little shoe of Thelma's that she was just putting by--and, smoothing her curls, went down to her supper ... Lady Winsleigh shrinks from that frank and childlike openness of regard? Why does she, for one brief moment, hate herself?... the first genuine blush ... suddenly spreads a hot and embarrassing tide of crimson ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal personality and feeling with intimate, specific actions (kissing a shoe, smoothing curls, a furtive blush). Combine outward gestures with brief interior commentary to make characters' emotional states immediate and credible rather than told in abstract terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of distinctive dialogue/idiolect to mark class and personality
rubrics_metrics.description: Waal now! Dew tell! ... I thought yew were in Pa-ar--is! ... 'It is to blay I am here!' ... 'Ze celebrated Machtenklinken!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Render speech patterns, accent spelling, and colloquialisms to signal regional background, education level, or affectation. Contrast affected, nasal or provincial turns of phrase with cultivated, ironic diction to dramatize social divisions. Beware caricature that flattens rather than differentiates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conferring social status by observers' reactions and critics' endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: As soon as he was seen devoting his attention to the 'new beauty,' excited whispers began to flit from mouth to mouth,--'She will be the rage this season!'--'We must ask her to come to us!' ... The die was cast,--the authority of Beau Lovelace was nearly supreme ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show a character's ascent in society by staging the reactions of other characters and the approbation of an influential arbiter (critic, celebrity). Use gossip, whispering, and explicit praise to dramatize how reputation is manufactured socially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satirical narrator voice to expose hypocrisy and moral observation
rubrics_metrics.description: Modern society contains within itself the seed of its own destruction,--the most utter Nihilist that ever swore deadly oath need but contain his soul in patience ... For God's justice is as a circle that slowly surrounds an evil ... So let the babes of the world play on ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ a wry, sometimes moralizing narrator who interjects general observations and aphorisms to frame scenes and underline themes. Use sweeping statements and ironic distance to critique social mores; temper with concrete examples so the satire remains grounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character revelation by juxtaposition and contrast
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'fisherwoman' could speak French,--moreover, she could speak it with a wonderfully soft and perfect accent,--the 'person' had studied Homer and Shakespeare, and was conversant with the best literature ... every costume looked tawdry beside her richly flowing velvet draperies ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reveal a character's depth and the shock they create by contrasting prior assumptions (peasant, uneducated) with demonstrated cultivation, taste, and presence. Let other characters' surprise and jealousy show the social implications of that contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray artists/critics with epigrammatic opinion to define literary debates
rubrics_metrics.description: 'So many apparently lofty and pathetic tragedies turn out, on close examination, to be the meanest and most miserable of farces ... it's the fashion nowadays to be chiffonniers in literature--to pick up the rags of life and sort them ... What's the use of spending thought and care on the manufacture of a jewelled diadem, and offering it ... when they prefer an olla-podrida of cast-off clothing ...'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give writer/critic characters witty, sharply formulated pronouncements that reveal their aesthetic stance; use metaphor and provocation ('chiffonnier', 'olla-podrida') to dramatize literary conflicts and social taste. Such lines both characterize the speaker and orient reader toward thematic debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evoking atmosphere with sensory specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: There is the rustle of silk and satin,--perfume, shaken out of lace kerchiefs, and bouquets oppresses the warm air,--the heat is excessive,--and there is a never-ending monotonous hum of voices ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-sensory details (sound of rustling fabrics, perfume, oppressive heat, hum of voices) to make crowded interiors palpable. Layer sensory impressions to communicate mood (oppressiveness, artificial warmth) rather than relying solely on visual description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose social maneuvering through formal introductions and polite cruelty
rubrics_metrics.description: I must find you some people to talk to. This is my dear friend, Mrs. Rush-Marvelle--I am sure you will like each other. Let me introduce Mrs. Van Clupp to you--Mrs. Van Clupp, and Miss Van Clupp!' ... 'Sir Francis Lennox'--continues Lady Winsleigh, and there is something like a sneer in her smile ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the ritualized language of introductions, name-dropping, and the measured gallantry of hosts/hostesses to reveal underlying rivalries, malice, and social arbitration. Small tonal cues (a sneer, a tightening of lips) convert ordinary politeness into narrative tension.
